summary: Turns the v2 "reuse ba:skill_purchasingagent" Store Manager into TWO (optionally three) genuinely native hired roles — Filiaalmanager (sm:skill_storemanager), Team Leader (sm:skill_teamleader), and later Assistant Manager (sm:skill_assistantmanager) — each with its own custom SkillData, job title, wage scale, Recruitment-Agency hireability, and its own HQ BizMan tab. The v2 supervision LOGIC (mod-owned StoreManagerPlan in GameInstance.modData, weekly DeliveryContract restock, snapshot/restore, feedback, read-only-on-corrupt) is kept almost verbatim and re-parented from the reused skill onto sm:skill_storemanager. Everything new rides on bundled Harmony (Dependencies/0Harmony.dll): a re-inject of runtime-built SkillData into SkillHelper.Skills, a defense-in-depth Postfix on SkillHelper.GetData, and a Postfix on BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs that builds the tab UI at runtime. Every Harmony surface is gated on GameVersion.buildNumber + non-null reflection handles and degrades to the existing permanent ModOptions panel. Departments are mod-invented (a named bucket of product itemNames within one store); Team Leader raises per-department restock requests, Store Manager merges + trims them to the store budget and writes ONE contract. D10 ("no custom skill") is overridden; D9/D12/D13/D14 stand. Phase A (custom Store Manager skill + hire + GetData guard, panel stays) is fully specified and buildable now.
customSkills:
THREE skill ids (Team Leader + Store Manager designed now, Assistant Manager Phase D): sm:skill_teamleader, sm:skill_assistantmanager, sm:skill_storemanager. All lowercase, "sm:" prefix, no enum — skills are 100% string-keyed (enums.txt cannot add a usable value).

RUNTIME SkillData (no asset bundle in Phase A). In Interop/SkillRegistry.cs, per skill:
  var sd = ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>();       // BigAmbitions.Characters.Skills.SkillData : TaggedScriptableObject
  sd.skillName = id;  sd.name = id;
  sd.baseHourlyWage = TL 18f / AM 21f / SM 24f;                // starting constants — Phase D tunes against a runtime dump of vanilla baselines
  sd.trainingCostMultiplier = 1f;
  sd.secondarySkill = string.Empty;                            // MUST be empty — short-circuits every secondarySkillRange read
  sd.secondarySkillRange = new Vector2Int(5,20);
  sd.associatedColorGradient = new Gradient(); sd.associatedColorGradient.SetKeys(new[]{new GradientColorKey(<roleColor>,0f),new GradientColorKey(<roleColor>,1f)}, new[]{new GradientAlphaKey(1f,0f),new GradientAlphaKey(1f,1f)});  // MUST be non-null — ScheduleHelper.GetEmployeeColor calls .Evaluate() unconditionally
  sd.possibleDealbreakers = new List<string>();
  sd.icon28 = null;                                            // tolerated everywhere (Image with null sprite renders nothing); Phase D loads a PNG via Sprite.Create
  try { sd.BuildTagCache(); } catch { /* tagless instance -> HasTag()==false for all tags, which is the SAFE default for HQ-plan roles (no forced full-time, no job demands) */ }

WAGE LADDER = baseHourlyWage alone. Final wage = baseHourlyWage * (Mathf.Pow(skillValue,1.05f)/100f + 1f) * gameVariables.employeeHourlySalaryMultiplier. Agency candidates arrive at skill 20 (boost ~1.23). Targets: employee ~$16 (vanilla ba:skill_customerservice), Team Leader ~$22 (base 18 -> ~22 at v20), Assistant ~$26 (base 21), Store Manager ~$30 (base 24 -> ~29.5 at v20, ~38 at v50). No secondarySkill so secondSkillValue is never consulted.

RE-INJECT HOOK (SkillHelper.Skills is private static readonly Dictionary<string,SkillData>, wiped + rebuilt by OnSkillDataLoaded on every save-load / new-game, no mod-merge step):
  - PRIMARY: Harmony Postfix on SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded(IList<SkillData>) -> SkillRegistry.EnsureInjected().
  - BACKSTOP: [ModEntryOnCityLoad] StoreManagerCityMod.OnLoadAsync also calls EnsureInjected() (runs after AddressableLoader, before gameplay).
  EnsureInjected(): reflect typeof(SkillHelper).GetField("Skills", NonPublic|Static) ONCE, cache the dict reference (only ever .Clear()/.Add()ed, never reassigned), then dict[id] = cachedSkillData for each id. Idempotent.

HARMONY GUARD (defense-in-depth; the real fix is the injection):
  [HarmonyPatch(typeof(SkillHelper), nameof(SkillHelper.GetData), new[]{typeof(string)})]
  static void Postfix(string skillName, ref SkillData __result){ if (__result == null) __result = SkillRegistry.Fallback(skillName); }   // Fallback returns the same cached object, or null for a non-mod id
  Second overload [HarmonyPatch(typeof(SkillHelper),"GetData",new[]{typeof(Skill)})] Postfix(Skill skill, ref SkillData __result){ if (__result==null) __result = SkillRegistry.Fallback(skill.name); }
This alone neutralises all ~15 unguarded GetData(...).member sites (wage calc EmployeeHelper.cs:353/361, training cost :452, RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate:65, JobDemandHelper:124/142, HeadhunterPlan:74/108/138, RecruitmentSettings:126, RecruitmentAgencyDialog:158, ScheduleEmployeeInfoBox:60 icon28, ScheduleHelper:142 gradient, CompatibilityFixes EA03).
hiring:
Recruitment Agency does NOT "just work" from a SkillHelper registration — the agency skill dropdown = BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills INTERSECT RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills, neither derived from SkillHelper. Interop/RecruitmentWiring.cs.EnsureAgencySkills() (called from city load, optionally also a Harmony Postfix on BusinessTypeHelper.OnBusinessTypesLoaded):
  1. BusinessTypeHelper.GetData("ba:businesstype_headquarters").employeePrimarySkills — reflect the string[], append sm:skill_storemanager / sm:skill_teamleader (/ assistantmanager) if absent, write back an appended copy. This is the SAME array ba:skill_purchasingagent already lives in, so the two roles are recruited exactly where the Purchasing Agent is: an Agency campaign with the HQ business selected.
  2. Every recruitment-agency BuildingRegistration -> ((RecruitmentAgencySettings)building.SpecialService.settings).availableEmployeeSkills — append the same ids.
  Both idempotent (contains-check); re-applied every city load (Addressables reload wipes them).
Headhunter path is FREE: HeadhuntersRecruitingTab.SetUpSkillsToRecruitArray iterates SkillHelper.AllSkillNames, so an injected skill auto-appears in the headhunter dropdown (leave it — do NOT add to HeadhunterHelper.skillsToSkipWhenRecruiting).
FALLBACK if array mutation fails: a mod "Recruit a Store Manager" action in the ModOptions panel / console that calls Helpers.RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate("sm:skill_storemanager", 20f, hqAddressObj, null, 0f) directly — bypasses the agency dropdown entirely; the candidate then flows through the normal My-Employees Candidates -> HireCandidate path unchanged.

MY EMPLOYEES TITLE: the displayed job title is the primary-skill id string run through Localizor (the loc key IS the skill id, verbatim, no transform). Ship in Locales/en.json + Locales/nl.json:
  "sm:skill_storemanager": "Store Manager"      (nl: "Filiaalmanager")
  "sm:skill_teamleader":  "Team Leader"          (nl: "Teamleider")
  "sm:skill_assistantmanager": "Assistant Manager" (nl: "Assistent-filiaalmanager")
ModLifecycleLoader re-runs LocalizorManager.LoadLocalizationTables after every mod load, so the Locales/ folder is picked up automatically. My Employees list rows, the detail card skill rows, and the filter chips are all fully dynamic (EmployeeFilterController iterates SkillHelper.AllSkillNames) — no UI patch. RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate's skill->subclass switch falls through to plain EmployeeInstance for an unknown skill (identical to ba:skill_purchasingagent) — acceptable; no subclass, no Harmony on that switch (the mod's ManagerDirectory.Reconcile already handles fire/unschedule cleanup).
HireCandidate is entirely skill-agnostic (no GetData anywhere) — once a candidate object exists, hiring works for any skill string.
hqExpansion:
There is NO native HQ level / size / tier / desk-cap / manager-cap mechanic. "Expanding the Headquarters" is two concrete things:

1. REQUIRED PLUMBING (Interop/HqDeskWiring.cs.EnsureDeskSkills(), city load, idempotent, re-applied each load): append sm:skill_storemanager / sm:skill_teamleader (/ assistantmanager) to the suitableSkills string[] of ItemsGetter.GetByName("ba:itemname_desktopcomputer" | "ba:itemname_laptop" | "ba:itemname_computer"). Without this, ScheduleHelper.HasSkillForWorkstation rejects the custom-skill manager at a vanilla HQ desk (WorkShiftDrag error bizman_schedule_employee_doesnt_have_required_skill) and the plan can never gate on IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift(). Those desks already carry the vanilla manager skills (which are in the HQ BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills) so they still pass GetAssignableItems()'s intersection test after we append. FALLBACK if array mutation fails: a small Harmony Prefix on ScheduleHelper.HasSkillForWorkstation returning true for our skill ids at HQ desks; or degrade to the v2 skipScheduleCheck path (plan active whenever the manager is hired + assignedAddress==HQ, no real shift required).

2. MOD-INVENTED CAPACITY (pure bookkeeping, no patch): 1 Store Manager per HQ (apex, fixed). Team Leader capacity = f(HQ state) — GameApi.GetAssignableDeskCount(hq) (BuildingRegistration.GetAssignableItems().Count) OR 1 + floor(BuildingSizeHelper.GetData(hqReg).squareMeters / X). Enforced in the mod's own assign UI; when full, Notifications.Show(Warning, "sm:hq_full") + the phone Contact: "HQ full — rent a larger office or add desks." So "expand the HQ" = the player physically rents a bigger office and/or places more desktopcomputer/laptop items, and the mod reads squareMeters / desk count to allow more Team Leaders.

REJECTED: faking a BuildingSize / BuildingVersion change — there is no mutation path, and it would desync rent, security, marketing reach, and by-sqm business requirements. BAModAPI exposes no buildingsize/item/skill registration API. Plan storage needs no "expansion" — vanilla plan lists are uncapped and our state is in modData.
hierarchy:
Ladder: store employee -> Team Leader -> (Assistant Manager) -> Store Manager.

TEAM LEADER: owns one DEPARTMENT of one store. Its job is to raise a per-department restock REQUEST each week: for every product itemName in the department, weeklyDemand = DeliveryContractItem.amountOrderedLastWeek (real units the game delivered last week — NEVER the contract line's own current amount, that is the D12 compounding trap), onHand = BuildingHelper.CountTotalResourcesInStock, proposed = weeklyDemand + min(gap, weeklyDemand) toward targetDays. Output: Dictionary<itemName,int>. The Team Leader is a real hired sm:skill_teamleader employee scheduled at the HQ; a Team-Leader plan slot = Department.TeamLeaderEmployeeId. Its store-cap contribution to the department is skill-scaled but there is no "N stores" — a TL is bound to exactly one department of one store.

STORE MANAGER: supervises N stores (N = MaxStoresForSkill(skill) = 1 + floor(skill/25), unchanged from v2). Each week it APPROVES the buying: sum every Team-Leader request for a store per itemName, apply StoreAssignment.WeeklyRestockBudgetCap, trim if over budget (order: department Priority desc, then pro-rata within a priority band, then primary-products-first), then write the MERGED per-line targets into that store's ONE DeliveryContract. Departments are a bookkeeping layer ABOVE the single contract — never separate contracts. A store with no departments = one implicit whole-store department, planner uses the existing v2 ComputeTarget path unchanged.

ASSISTANT MANAGER: its own custom skill sm:skill_assistantmanager (for title + wage tier ~$26 + Agency hireability), but NOT its own plan and NOT its own HQ tab. Modelled as StoreManagerPlan.AssistantManagerEmployeeId — a single optional delegate attached to a Store Manager plan, managed from the Store Managers tab. Effect: (a) +1 to the Store Manager's MaxStores and +1 Team-Leader capacity; (b) optionally covers the weekly approval pass when the Store Manager is Dormant (sick / unscheduled), so the plan keeps running. If (b) proves fiddly against Reconcile's dormant/active notifications, drop it — the assistant then only raises capacity (simplest correct behaviour). Phase D.
departmentModel:
The game has NO department / section / zone / aisle concept (re-confirmed Build 3672 — the only "Zone" types are outdoor spawn zones; SchedulePartitioner.SchedulePartition is a transient auto-scheduler grouping, not persisted, not player-facing). Grouping "by game product category" is INFEASIBLE (no categories). "Subset of stations" is INFEASIBLE as a stock model (showcase shelves aren't assignable, registers aren't product-scoped).

MODEL (option a — mod-owned named bucket of product itemNames, Domain/Department.cs):
  [Serializable] sealed class Department {
    string Name;                       // "Fresh", "Ambient", "Frozen" — player-named
    string StoreAddress;
    List<string> ProductItemNames;     // picked from BusinessType.GetAllProducts()/GetPrimaryProducts() for that store
    List<string> ShelfInstanceIds;     // OPTIONAL opt-in spatial tagging; self-healing
    string TeamLeaderEmployeeId;
    int Priority;                      // for over-budget trim order
    bool Dormant;                      // TL gone/unscheduled -> this dept falls back to whole-store planning
  }
Hangs off StoreAssignment as List<Department> Departments, same GameInstance.modData blob, same Serialization.Envelope (public fields, Odin Everything policy covers the new nested type).

SEEDING (so a player who doesn't care still gets a working setup): on first "enable departments" for a store, offer — (1) one department = all primary products (GetPrimaryProducts()), or (2) auto-split primary products into N even chunks. Player then edits membership via a multi-toggle in the Team Leiders tab.

OPTIONAL SPATIAL FLAVOR: also let the player tag ShowcaseShelf ItemInstance ids (enumerate BuildingRegistration.GetItemsOfType(ItemType.ShowcaseShelf) + GetStockInstance().itemName) into a department and derive ProductItemNames from what's on those shelves. Instance ids churn on remodel -> self-healing: on load, drop unknown ids and fall back to the product-name list (the robust core). Keep this opt-in.

No Harmony, no game entity, no fake items, no scheduler patch — departments are invisible to the game; they only shape what the Store Manager writes into the one DeliveryContract. Reads are all public: BusinessType.GetAllProducts/GetPrimaryProducts, GetItemsOfType, ItemInstance.GetStockInstance, DeliveryContractItem.amountOrderedLastWeek, CountTotalResourcesInStock.

CAVEAT: a store can have multiple DeliveryContracts (one per wholesaler); v2 grabs the first. Decide a rule in Phase C — standardize on one contract per store, or split merged requests across the right contracts by which wholesaler stocks each itemName.

Mitigation: TeamLeaderRequests and the approved-targets PlanAndApply overload read ONLY amountOrderedLastWeek + CountTotalResourcesInStock; a store with no readable product list degrades to a single implicit whole-store department using the proven v2 ComputeTarget.

risks: Custom-skill fragility across game updates: ~15 unguarded SkillHelper.GetData(...).member call sites; a Build 3673 signature change to SkillHelper, BizManBusiness, RecruitmentAgencySettings, or the HQ desk item names breaks a patch. Mitigated by the build-number gate ([3600,3899]) + non-null-handle checks + graceful degrade to the ModOptions panel and (worst case) the v2 ba:skill_purchasingagent path.

SkillHelper.Skills is wiped + rebuilt on every save-load, new-game, and city load with no mod-merge step. The re-inject MUST land before the first consumer. If the Harmony Postfix on OnSkillDataLoaded fails to apply, there is a window between the reload and the [ModEntryOnCityLoad] backstop where candidate generation / wage calc for a custom-skill employee could NPE — order matters; the GetData Postfix is the safety net for that window.

Employees saved with a custom primary skill store fine as {name,value}, but if the mod is later UNINSTALLED while such employees exist, vanilla SkillHelper.GetData NPEs on the player's save (wage calc, employee card, compat fixes). Must ship an OnUnloadAsync cleanup that re-skills active sm:skill_* employees to ba:skill_purchasingagent, and document 'fire your custom-role staff before removing the mod'.

BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs patch clones the live PurchasingAgents menu-button prefab blind (hierarchy not in the decomp); a visually broken button is possible. Gate + try/catch + DestroyImmediate + fall back to the panel.

TaggedScriptableObject / TagRef internals are in an un-decompiled assembly. BuildTagCache() on a runtime instance may throw or leave HasTag() unreliable. Accepted: HasTag()==false for all tags is the safe default for HQ-plan roles (no forced full-time, no job demands, no store work-shift requirement).

Department merge/trim approval is 100% mod-arbitrated and can re-introduce the D12 geometric-compounding bug if any code path bases a target on the DeliveryContract line's own current amount instead of amountOrderedLastWeek. Enforced by only ever reading amountOrderedLastWeek + CountTotalResourcesInStock.

A store can hold multiple DeliveryContracts (one per wholesaler); v2 uses the first. Departments must standardize on one contract per store or split merged requests by wholesaler — an unresolved design choice for Phase C.

Two installed mods bundling different Harmony majors share whichever assembly loads first (ModAssemblyLoader caches by simple name). Use a unique Harmony id string, ship a current 2.3.x, never assume the in-memory Harmony is our copy.

Wage baselines for shipped skills are in un-decompiled ScriptableObjects; Phase A ships approximate baseHourlyWage constants and Phase D tunes them against a runtime dump — the ladder may read wrong until then.

RecruitmentAgencySettings may be one shared Addressable asset or per-building copies, and it re-loads per city — RecruitmentWiring must re-apply every city load and cannot assume a single mutation sticks.

The HQ 'Team Leader capacity' formula reads GetAssignableItems().Count / squareMeters live; a player mid-remodel (desks temporarily removed) could see capacity drop below current assignments — Reconcile must tolerate over-capacity gracefully (freeze new assigns, never auto-drop).
